insights.title: Fewer downpours than before
insights.body: Days with 20 mm or more of rain went from about 74 to 65 a year (first vs last 10 years).

insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 0 to 3 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rice, Salt-tolerant rice and Soybean score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: Crops will need about 763 mm more water than rain gives
consequences.detail: Rain minus crop water demand moves from 3,156 mm to about 2,393 mm a year.
consequences.action: Plan irrigation or water harvesting, or shift to crops that need less water.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 3,604 mm
consequences.detail: That is 16% below the 4,290 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: +0.6 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 26.0 °C to about 26.6 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
